evidence: The hazard is real: show_cmd holds seed.profile_lock across an unbounded osascript call that can wait on a TCC consent dialog. The supporting claim that the codebase bounds every blocking external call is overstated, as the agent showed with chrome.scan's untimed ps call.
guidance_note: When a subprocess call runs inside a held lock, ask whether it can block on a human, and bound it before the first push.

evidence: Only FileNotFoundError was caught around subprocess.run, so PermissionError escaped as a traceback. The agent noted chrome.launch already catches OSError around its Popen.
guidance_note: When wrapping a new subprocess call, copy the exception breadth the existing sibling wrapper (chrome.launch's OSError) already uses.

evidence: The reviewer was asking whether to confirm fail-fast versus aggregation. Fail-fast is defensible, and the error names the failing pid. The real gap was that no test pinned the multi-pid failure case, which the agent closed with test_a_pid_that_cannot_be_raised_fails_the_whole_command.
guidance_note: When behavior falls out of sum() over a generator, pin the multi-element failure case with a test so the decision is explicit.

evidence: Both new commands call session.working(ref), which auto-declares, but the README enumeration listed only up/port/env/mcp/config. Fixed in 48a2ab9.
guidance_note: When adding a command that goes through a shared path, grep the README for enumerations of that path's callers.

evidence: This duplicates F1: the same missing osascript timeout inside the profile lock, fixed by the same RAISE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS change in e90b7d6. The reviewer hedged on whether macOS actually blocks headless, and the agent's reply corrects the same overstated premise.
guidance_note: When a subprocess call runs inside a held lock, ask whether it can block on a human, and bound it before the first push.

evidence: In the original show_cmd the 'Started' line was built only after window.raise_profile returned, so a -1743 raise failure hid the launch. The agent echoed it to stderr before the raise instead of folding it into the error. The 48a2ab9 diff shows this and a test pins it.
guidance_note: In a command that does two effects in sequence, report the first effect before attempting the second so a later failure cannot hide it.

evidence: The original message used pids[0] for the new browser while joining every stopped pid. The 48a2ab9 diff changes it to join every pid, and the reply-hint 'pushback' is lexical noise because the agent accepted.
guidance_note: When one message reports two values of the same type, render both through the same expression.

evidence: This duplicates F7 (pids[0] versus a joined stopped list) and was fixed by the same 48a2ab9 change with test_restart_names_every_pid_on_both_sides_of_the_message.
guidance_note: When one message reports two values of the same type, render both through the same expression.

evidence: The original show_cmd emitted only profile.describe() even though the human line branched on windows. The 48a2ab9 diff adds started and windows alongside the record.
guidance_note: When the human output branches on a value, check that the --json payload carries that value too.

evidence: The original restart_cmd JSON carried only the new pids, so a --json caller could not tell a replace from a fresh start. The 48a2ab9 diff adds 'stopped' to the payload.
guidance_note: When the human output branches on a value, check that the --json payload carries that value too.

evidence: chrome.launch's _Answered arm returned find_pids() unchecked, so an empty tuple could reach pids[0]. The reviewer hedged on reachability. Fixing at the source in launch was the right call, but the first version (368553d) raised directly and skipped the shared cleanup, which seeded F12, F14, F15 and F16.
guidance_note: When adding a new failure ending to a match whose sibling arms all end through a shared cleanup-and-raise, route the new arm through that same tail.

evidence: F11's fix added a raise CromError in the _Answered arm that bypassed _stop_after_failure, which every sibling arm uses, leaving a live CDP-answering browser running. d5d5ba4 routes it through the shared ending with demand=_still_held rather than the reviewer's _port_held, with a test that the second scan's pid is signalled.
guidance_note: When adding a failure arm to launch, read how the sibling arms end and reuse the shared stop-after-failure path instead of raising on the spot.

evidence: F6's fix echoed 'Started' before the raise in show_cmd only. restart_cmd has the same shape (kill, then a start that can raise), and its stop fact was still lost until d5d5ba4 echoed 'Stopped ...' before _start_under_lock.
guidance_note: After fixing an effect-then-failure info-loss in one command, sweep every command built on the same two-step shape (here restart alongside show).

evidence: d5d5ba4 kept the message 'crom can neither report nor stop it' while routing the arm through _escalate, which the new test shows can and does stop the browser. The agent dropped the false clause in 07fe23c.
guidance_note: When changing what an error path does, reread the message text it raises against the new behavior.

evidence: F11's fix added a fourth failure ending to launch while the docstring still said 'The three ways that can go wrong'. The agent removed the count and added the fourth next step instead of bumping the number.
guidance_note: When adding an arm to a match, grep the enclosing docstring for a count or enumeration of the arms.

evidence: F12's fix chose _still_held over _port_held, but setUp stubs _port_is_free=True, so the port half was never exercised. The agent confirmed that swapping the demand left the suite green, then added a test that discriminates.
guidance_note: When a fix picks one option over another for a stated reason, add a test that fails under the rejected option.

evidence: 48a2ab9 (the F9/F10 fixes) added stopped, started and windows to the JSON payloads without touching the README's --json section. 0ff0665 then documented them.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a documented output shape, update the README section that documents that shape in the same commit.

evidence: The finding assumes CliRunner's mix_stderr defaults to True. The agent showed Click 8.3.1 has no mix_stderr parameter and captures stdout and stderr separately, with the json.loads on .stdout succeeding. The flag is a false positive because the flagged test is correct and no defect exists.

The browser being stopped was launched by this same call seconds earlier, so 'any open tabs' cannot exist. _NeverAnswered already SIGTERMs a live process silently under the same convention. The flag is a false positive: the finding exists only because F12 routed this arm through cleanup, and there is no defect.

_start_under_lock's 'rather than printing anything' was false from the original PR, because the function echoes 'Creating ... from seed' to stderr. The flag on 0ff0665 is a false positive: the docstring and the echo predate review, and no fix commit touched them.
guidance_note: Before writing a docstring claim about what a function does not do (prints, mutates), grep its body for that effect.

evidence: A non-zero osascript return with empty stderr produced 'could not raise ... (pid N): ' with nothing after the colon. This is the original returncode branch: F2's fix touched only the except OSError arm, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When building an error message from captured stderr, always include the exit status so an empty stderr still yields a diagnostic.

narrative: Round 0 raised eleven largely valid findings, and the agent handled them well, moving the empty-pids fix to its source. That source fix raised on the spot instead of using launch's shared stop-after-failure tail, which produced a chain across rounds 1 and 2: the leak (F12), the stale message (F14), the stale arm count (F15) and an untested demand choice (F16). F6's fix was also applied to show but not to restart (F13), and the new JSON keys went undocumented (F17). Round 3's valid findings (F20, F21) were pre-existing code the reviewer missed earlier, and its other finding (F19) and round 2's F18 were correctly rejected.
guidance_observations: The two duplicate pairs (F1/F5, F7/F8) were answered consistently without wasted rework.
Each fix that added a new failure arm or output key needed a sweep of its siblings: other arms' cleanup tail, the arm count in the docstring, the README shape section, and the parallel command.
The agent ran the suite against the reviewer's mix_stderr claim instead of conceding, which stopped a wrong change from shipping.

evidence: entry_key had no length cap while the file's own comment derived a roughly 30-character budget, and 64-character namespaces are legal. The agent raised rather than truncating, because truncation breaks injectivity, and pulled in a ticket it had deferred.
guidance_note: When a comment derives a budget, enforce that budget in the code that consumes it in the same change rather than filing it for later.

evidence: 2798d5a made entry_key raise CromError inside write(), whose docstring promised only ValueError. The agent unified on CromError and removed mcp_cmd's ValueError translation instead of documenting two error types.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new raise inside a function, reread the caller's documented raise surface and except clauses in the same commit.

evidence: F1's fix tested the refusal only at entry_key, not through write(), where the contract is that the file is left untouched. The agent added test_rejects_a_ref_it_cannot_spell and checked that it fails under the reordering the reviewer described.
guidance_note: When adding a new refusal to a function with sibling refusal tests, add one in the same shape asserting the same end state.

narrative: One valid round-0 finding: the new derived key had no length budget. The fix was correct but left write()'s documented raise surface stale and tested the refusal only one layer down, which cost round 1. The agent fixed the doc drift by removing the second error type rather than documenting it.
guidance_observations: The agent had filed the length cap as a deferred ticket instead of fixing it in the PR that introduced the hazard, which is what made round 0 necessary.

evidence: The broad except OSError caught EPIPE before click's handler. The agent reproduced it (exit 120 plus 'Error: Broken pipe') and carved out errno.EPIPE instead of BrokenPipeError, because the latter also covers ESHUTDOWN, which click would decline. Both mutations were run to confirm the tests discriminate.
guidance_note: When broadening an except clause at a boundary, check which subclasses the framework's outer handler relies on catching (click's EPIPE arm).

evidence: The chrome.py and configwrite.py comments became false. The config.py comment was about UnicodeDecodeError, a ValueError, so only its parenthetical was stale. The agent reworded each site to its local reason, but only the three named sites (d311d9f), which left the class unswept.
guidance_note: When a boundary change falsifies a comment class, grep for the phrase ('exit-code contract', 'catches only CromError') across the repo rather than fixing the named instances.

evidence: d311d9f fixed only the three comments F2 named. Three more in cli.py, plus ten others the agent then found by grep in f6f50ca, still claimed a raw OSError escapes as a traceback. The agent conceded it 'fixed the three comments the review named and left the class alone'.
guidance_note: When a boundary change falsifies a comment class, grep for the phrase ('exit-code contract', 'catches only CromError') across the repo rather than fixing the named instances.

evidence: f6f50ca's rewrite of migrate.py added 'a list of triples naming no profile', which is copytree's Error shape. shutil.move's self-nesting raises a single formatted string, and the agent confirmed this against the interpreter.
guidance_note: When rewording a comment, do not add new factual detail about a library's behavior unless you checked it on that exact call path.

evidence: f6f50ca reworded chrome.kill's docstring to 'reported after rm had already undeclared the profile', dropping the past-tense verb. That made historical behavior read as current, contradicting rm_cmd's delete-before-undeclare ordering.
guidance_note: When cutting a clause from a sentence that narrates history, check that the tense survives in what remains.

evidence: CPython sets only LC_CTYPE from the environment, so strerror stays untranslated without an explicit setlocale. The agent measured this on macOS only, but the reasoning holds. The agent disputed the premise yet switched to os.strerror(errno.X) on independent grounds. The test was in the original PR rather than a fix commit, so the flag is a false positive.

Path.exists() swallows ENOTDIR, so the afile/x.json case fails in write_text like case 2, not 'before either'. The agent confirmed this against the interpreter. The docstring dates from the original PR's test, not a fix commit, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Before a docstring states which call a failure comes from, run the case and read the traceback.

narrative: Round 0 found a real EPIPE regression, which was well handled, and a class of stale comments. The agent fixed only the three named comment instances, so round 1 found three more (F3). The full sweep in f6f50ca then introduced two new inaccuracies in reworded comments: an invented shutil.Error shape (F4) and a lost past tense (F5). Round 3's F6 and F7 were on original test code.
guidance_observations: The comment-sweep fix was itself the largest source of new findings, so a rewrite of thirteen comments needed the same fact-checking as new code.
The agent's practice of running mutations and interpreter checks before accepting or rejecting kept every response choice correct.

evidence: migrate.run_if_needed and _bootstrap_user_config run in the group callback before the subcommand's --json is parsed. The agent rejected raw-argv detection because it gives a false positive when '--json' is another option's value. It replaced the rationalizing comment, pinned the limitation with a test, and filed crom-contract-oen.7 for moving that work out of the group callback.
guidance_note: When a feature promises behavior 'for every failure', list every place a failure can originate (including the group callback) before writing the claim.

evidence: The envelope write in _Failure.show ran inside click's except ClickException handler, outside the EPIPE arm. The agent reproduced exit 120 with a traceback, then moved the write into the boundary (_answer) instead of adding a second EPIPE guard.
guidance_note: When adding a stdout write on a failure path, check whether it runs inside the region the EPIPE carve-out from crom#30 protects.

narrative: Two valid round-0 findings, both answered with structurally better fixes than the reviewer suggested. The argv-scan suggestion was correctly declined for a documented boundary plus a ticket. Round 1 approved with no fix-caused findings.
guidance_observations: F2 repeats the EPIPE class crom#30 had just fixed, so the agent's own prior fix was not carried forward as a check when adding a new stdout write.
